claim: Wald's SPRT stops when the likelihood ratio crosses one of two bounds set by the target error rates (A=(1-b)/a, B=b/(1-a)); it is the point-prior case of a general evidence-ratio framework (a Bayes factor with point priors reduces to it).
agent_test: Implement SPRT stop on vote counts; check realised error against nominal at equal tokens.

claim: SPRT is optimal: among all tests with the same error bounds it has the smallest expected sample size (Wald-Wolfowitz 1948). The popular 'about half the samples' figure is from memory and was not verified from the original. Gap search: the original papers were still not opened (publisher bot-check, d20).
agent_test: Do not rely on the factor; measure the saving on our own task mix.

claim: Checking a fixed-sample test repeatedly and stopping at first success inflates false positives (fivefold at 10,000 samples in the Johari A/B setting, re-opened; Armitage 1969 figures of about 14% after 5 looks and 19% after 10 looks at nominal 5% are from memory only).
agent_test: Simulate: agent stops when answers look agreed (ad hoc) vs a pre-set rule; compare false-accept rate on known-wrong items.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Anytime-valid methods (mixture SPRT, confidence sequences, e-values) keep error guarantees under optional stopping. Mixture variance can be misspecified by two orders of magnitude with under 5% power loss and under 10% run-length cost; beyond that the cost reaches 20% power and 40% run-length (re-opened).
agent_test: Use a mixture rule instead of a single p1 in the vote stop; sweep prior width at equal tokens.

claim: Sequential designs cut expected sample size by 50% or more versus fixed-sample designs in human research (Stefan et al. 2022 review).
agent_test: Context only; measure savings on the LLM directly.

claim: Self-consistency (40 samples, majority vote) beats greedy chain of thought: GSM8K +17.9, SVAMP +11.0, AQuA +12.2 points. Re-checked in the paper. This is the fixed-budget baseline for all stopping work.
agent_test: Baseline arm at fixed N.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Stopping self-consistency when the leader is stable saves 2x to 8x samples at under 0.5 points accuracy loss: Adaptive-Consistency 3.3x on math (73.2 vs 73.1), 7.9x best case, GPT-3.5 4.4x; ESC saves 34-84% of samples. Both re-opened and confirmed.
agent_test: Add a Beta-posterior stop to the N-sample arm; report accuracy at matched average samples.

claim: At equal average sample cost, adaptive stopping is more accurate than fixed-n self-consistency (about +3 points on GSM8K at 10 samples, up to +5 elsewhere), so part of the gain is reallocating samples to hard items, not only skipping.
agent_test: Matched-cost comparison, adaptive vs fixed n.

claim: Savings shrink for weaker or more diffuse models: Vicuna-13B 1.9x vs GPT-3.5 4.4x; ESC on MATH cap 64: GPT-4 uses 42.4 of 64 samples, Llama-2-7b uses 62.5 (almost no saving). Re-opened. Gap search: against a fixed budget of 8 the saving is about 1 to 3.5 calls (GSM8K 8 to 4.5), at 4 the plain posterior rule saves 0 (d02).
agent_test: Report saving by model strength; expect little saving on hard items.

claim: A Wald SPRT on top-two answer counts (ConSol) cut tokens 63.9-88.7% vs 40-sample SC with equal or higher accuracy in most cells (AIME24 o3-mini-low 70.0 to 80.0; GPQA low: SC 68.2, SPRT 66.7, mSPRT 70.2). Table re-opened. One group, short-answer tasks only; authors state sensitivity to parameters. Gap search: reported results use p1=0.5001 and type-I tolerance alpha about 0.95, so the Wald error guarantee is void by design; mSPRT alpha was swept only over a 0.00018 window (d05).
agent_test: Replicate with our own p0/p1 on our tasks; test parameter sensitivity.

claim: SPRT beats the posterior-lead rule (Adaptive-Consistency) on token reduction at equal accuracy in ConSol's table (AIME24 high 84.5 vs 64.6; GSM 88.6 vs 82.8). Same authors ran both, so this is one source.
agent_test: Head-to-head AC vs SPRT, equal tokens, our tasks.

claim: Early stops are safe mainly where the model already agrees: DSC finds CoT and 40-sample SC agree on 84.8% (GPT-3.5) and 96.2% (GPT-4) of GSM8K items; difficulty-aware allocation cuts cost 65.29% / 56.04% vs SC and 24.81% / 21.86% vs ESC. Re-opened.
agent_test: One-sample first pass on easy items; escalate on disagreement.

claim: If the top answer's vote share is below 0.5, extra samples rarely help, so an early no-consensus stop is useful; ConSol reports most p1 values are above 0.5 for o3-mini.
agent_test: Log p1 at sample 10; if low, switch operator instead of drawing more votes.

claim: More votes can hurt: majority-vote accuracy is non-monotonic (inverse U) in number of calls on mixed easy/hard question sets (MMLU Physics, TruthfulQA, GPQA, AVeriTeC). Re-read: all real-data runs use GPT-3.5-turbo-0125 only; the peak depends on the easy/hard share, and synthetic optima were small (1 to 7 calls). Recent open and frontier-class models read (CGES 7B at B=4/8/16, DeepConf at 512 traces) show rises that flatten, not falls, but none was split by difficulty.
agent_test: Plot accuracy vs N by difficulty bucket on our items.

claim: Majority vote and reward-model selection plateau beyond several hundred samples even when coverage keeps rising (SWE-bench Lite 15.9% to 56% at 250 samples), so agreement-stopping cannot reach what only a verifier can pick.
agent_test: Where a checker exists, stop on verification, not on agreement.

claim: Weighting votes by the model's own confidence cuts needed samples by over 40% (CISC: P(True) 41% at budget 5, 46% at budget 10; plain SC needs 18.6 samples to match CISC at 10; Gemma2-9B on MATH 73%). Re-opened.
agent_test: Confidence-weighted vote vs plain vote at equal samples.

claim: Internal token confidence can drive early stopping: DeepConf reaches 99.9% on AIME25 (GPT-OSS-120B, offline @512; majority 97.0%, pass@1 91.8%) and online mode cuts tokens by up to 84.7%; consensus tau 0.95 keeps accuracy while 0.90 and 0.85 lose some. Headline and the 43-79% range re-opened; CORRECTION (gap search): the 62.88% mean (DeepConf-low) and 47.67% (DeepConf-high) vs majority voting on DeepSeek-8B IS in the paper, text under Figure 7. Needs per-token top-k log-probs inside the engine; not usable through a hosted API that hides them.
agent_test: Needs token log-probs; test if available.

claim: Reasoning-quality scoring (RASC) stops with about 70% fewer samples (ablation: answer-only 10.86 vs combined 8.20 generations); self-certainty distillation and path-consistency give 20-94% savings on plotted settings. Not re-opened.
agent_test: Only after answer-count stops are validated.

claim: Stopping inside a single chain: models reach their final answer after about 60% of steps on math; trial-answer confidence cuts CoT length 19.1-80.1% with accuracy +0.3 to +5.0. Two papers, not re-opened.
agent_test: Probe for answer at transition words; stop when stable.

claim: Casting repeated generation as optimal stopping (Pandora's box, UCB) gives the same quality as best-of-N with 15-35% fewer generations; savings grow with the quality target. Needs a reward model.
agent_test: Test with a cheap verifier.

claim: SPRT as a debate stop rule works only if the judge score separates useful from useless convergence. Morandi (2026, re-opened): GSM8K 1.01 rounds, 4.06 calls, 97.0% vs fixed-5 99.0% at 15 calls; MMLU hit the cap on 99.5% of items using 31.96 calls (2.1x fixed-5) because calibrated KL was about 0. The paper says no pairwise accuracy difference is significant (CI about 4.4 points) and single-round vote (3 calls) already reached 99.0% on GSM8K, so the saving against that cheap baseline is negative.
agent_test: Always include a cheap single-round baseline arm; require a KL check before using a judge-score SPRT.

claim: Savings come mainly from items where the model already agrees. No source tests stopping for open-ended generation, multi-step agent tasks, or correlated model errors. A confidently wrong consensus is the unmeasured failure case (DeepConf notes confident wrong traces). Gap search: between-model errors are strongly shared (60% agreement when both wrong, Helm, d12); the Certified SC certificate covers the model's mode only (d04); tau-bench shows run-to-run disagreement on agent tasks (d14); USC gives free-form agreement but no stop rule (d13). Still no direct false-stop measurement for single-model samples.
schema_part: G (stop only with an independent check)
agent_test: Seed questions with a common wrong answer; measure false-stop rate under each rule.

claim: Partial independent re-runs now exist for the posterior stop rules: CGES (UMass, 10 seeds, 7B models) re-ran ESC, Adaptive-Consistency and DSC; ESC and ASC saved about 40-45% of calls at B=16 within 0.4pp, ASC saved nothing at B=4. Blend-ASC (Noah's Ark) found Adaptive SC beaten by fixed allocation at budget 128 for the target it used. No independent test of ConSol's SPRT was found. Search limited (web quota exhausted, arXiv and Semantic Scholar rate limits).
agent_test: Run our own replication.

claim: At a small fixed budget the stop rule has little room: the posterior rule saved 0 of 4 calls and lost 0.5pp at B=4, about 1 to 3.5 of 8 calls at B=8, and 58% of 16 calls (CGES), 7B models, 10 seeds, calls not tokens.
agent_test: Compare stop vs fixed-5 and fixed-8 at equal tokens on our tasks.

claim: Agreement-stopping certifies the model's own mode, not the truth. Error floor is P(mode wrong); the cross-model shared-error rate is about 60% when both models are wrong (Helm). Same-model samples are likely more tied. Cross-model result is an upper reference, not a measured single-model false-stop rate.
schema_part: G (independent check before accepting unanimous stop)
agent_test: Seed items with a common wrong answer; measure the false-stop rate.

claim: No label-free threshold recipe exists. Textbook SPRT p1 0.55-0.6 was not what produced ConSol's savings (p1=0.5001, alpha about 0.95). Rigorous anytime-valid certificates are conservative (3-25% savings at the alphas tried). The Adaptive-Consistency 0.95 default is hand-set.
agent_test: Fit the threshold on a small labelled pilot; report accuracy vs p1 and alpha on a grid.

claim: Posterior-threshold stopping is fragile at high targets: Adaptive SC fell below fixed allocation at budget 128 (2.13x vs 3.40x) and failed to reach SC@128 on one model-set. Independent preprint, metric is reducible error vs the model's limiting mode.
agent_test: Plot accuracy vs average tokens for fixed, posterior and SPRT on our items.

claim: Verbalised 0-100 confidence recovers about two thirds of the saving of token-probability confidence (CISC cost cut 30% vs 46% at budget 10); DeepConf needs engine log-probs and is unavailable through hosted APIs that hide them (inference).
agent_test: Test verbalised confidence weighting on our task; compare with plain vote.

claim: For free-form output, agreement can be judged by the model (USC: TruthfulQA 62.1 to 67.7 on PaLM 2-L; 8 samples a sweet spot) but gives no vote share or stop rule; for agent tasks the usable agreement is final-state equality (tau-bench: pass^8 below 25% for the best agent).
agent_test: Build a pairwise 'same outcome' judge and measure its agreement with a human on 50 pairs.

claim: A one-sample or ranked difficulty probe is only moderately accurate (DSC ranking Spearman 0.62 GPT-4, 0.44 GPT-3.5 vs human labels) and the gate cost 1.9 to 3.1pp in an independent run. The miss rate on items where CoT and SC disagree has not been published.
agent_test: Measure the probe's miss rate on items where one sample and the vote disagree.

claim: When tests exist, stop at the first pass; majority vote plateaus (Llama-3-8B MATH 40.50 to 41.41% from 100 to 10,000 samples while coverage reaches 98.44%). Tests are imperfect (11.3% flaky SWE-bench Lite problems; 35 of 122 CodeContests problems with correct solutions failing tests), so keep a second check.
agent_test: Compare verify-stop with agree-stop on tasks with tests.

claim: A debate stability signal exists (KS distance on judge-correctness distribution below 0.05, stops in 2-8 of 10 rounds, accuracy change 0 to -1.03). Before trusting any convergence signal, check the calibrated KL between 'consensus' and 'no consensus' scores (GSM8K 9.80 vs MMLU about 0).
agent_test: Fit and report KL on 40+ labelled items before enabling the stop.

claim: SPRT error rates degrade gracefully with correlation in simulation: nominal 0.05 gave 0.015 at rho 0, 0.044 at 0.41, 0.065 at 0.6 (AR(1), 50,000 trajectories). Simulation only; Wald's and Wald-Wolfowitz's proofs for dependent streams were not opened.
agent_test: Do not claim error guarantees; measure empirical false-stop on our own vote streams.
